knowledge: Spastic paraplegia 93, autosomal recessive (SPG93, OMIM #620938) is an ultra-rare neurodegenerative condition caused by biallelic hypomorphic variants in the NFU1 gene, which encodes an iron-sulfur cluster scaffold protein essential for lipoic acid synthase and respiratory chain complexes. Historically, pathogenic NFU1 variants cause multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 1 (MMDS1, OMIM #605711), an infantile, rapidly fatal condition characterized by early lethality, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and pulmonary hypertension. SPG93 represents the milder, non-fatal, chronic end of the NFU1-related phenotypic spectrum, characterized primarily by childhood- to juvenile-onset progressive lower-extremity spasticity, hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses, and gait difficulty, often accompanied by complex features like cerebellar ataxia, mild cognitive or learning difficulties, dysarthria, and axonal or sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.
prior_hypothesis: Clinicians can differentiate SPG93 from other hereditary spastic paraplegias (such as SPG7, SPG11, SPG15, SPG35) and classical MMDS1 by identifying childhood/adolescent-onset progressive spastic paraplegia combined with subclinical or mild cerebellar signs and axonal neuropathy, but critically lacking the early-infantile fulminant pulmonary hypertension, severe lactic acidosis, and early lethality characteristic of classical MMDS1, while displaying neuroimaging evidence of subtle periventricular or deep white matter changes without extensive cavitating leukodystrophy.

candidate_answers.answer: Core clinical findings include progressive lower-limb spasticity, lower-limb hyperreflexia, and spastic gait (HPO: HP:0001258, HP:0001347, HP:0002064), reported in 100% of symptomatic individuals (estimated 4/4 to 8/8 across initial family descriptions), typically presenting in late childhood to early adulthood.
candidate_answers.aspect: Phenotypic spectrum and core motor presentation

candidate_answers.answer: Complex neurological features frequently observed include cerebellar ataxia (HPO: HP:0001251), dysarthria (HPO: HP:0001260), and distal axonal or sensorimotor polyneuropathy (HPO: HP:0009830), occurring in a majority of older affected patients.

Severe infantile pulmonary arterial hypertension (HPO: HP:0002092) and intractable metabolic lactic acidosis (HPO: HP:0003128), which are pathognomonic hallmarks of classical MMDS1, are absent in SPG93 patients, allowing direct clinical discrimination from canonical NFU1 deficiency.

Brain MRI in SPG93 demonstrates mild, non-cavitating periventricular T2/FLAIR white matter hyperintensities or thin corpus callosum, differing markedly from the profound cystic/cavitating leukoencephalopathy and basal ganglia necrosis seen in severe MMDS1.

Genotype-phenotype correlation exists where hypomorphic missense variants (preserving residual Fe-S cluster maturation activity) cause SPG93, whereas severe loss-of-function variants or the classic founder variant (e.g., p.Gly208Cys) in homozygosity lead to fulminant MMDS1.

assumptions: SPG93 is delineated in OMIM #620938 as an autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia caused by NFU1 variants.
The published literature on SPG93 is currently limited to a few index families/cohorts describing mild or adult-surviving NFU1 phenotypes.
Phenotypes described in classic MMDS1 literature are considered distinct in severity and presentation from SPG93, although they represent an allelic spectrum.
